_comment: Canonical PROCEDURAL semantics. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'how generated content is produced deterministically'. Procedural answers exactly two questions -- what seed does this frame/beat use, and how does a count become a layout/lattice -- and must NOT re-implement other subsystems' truth: drawing belongs to primitives (primitive_catalog.v1), time/easing to timeline (easing_vocabulary.v1), space/transform to geometry (transform_vocabulary.v1), motion timing to motion_canonical (motion_semantics.v2). Before this contract the video-level seed 20261003 was hard-coded in two producers (raster_renderer, visual_director) and slot math lived only in ref_frame while svg_art hand-rolled its lattice loops. See runtime/docs/procedural-inventory.md.

procedural_must_never: construct its own random.Random(...) outside procedural_canonical.rng
hard-code a seed literal outside procedural_canonical.rng
forge a lattice loop outside procedural_canonical.layout
depend on any non-stdlib runtime module (it is a leaf)

determinism._comment: A picture claim is only meaningful if the numbers behind it are reproducible across processes/machines. PYTHONHASHSEED must not leak into any seed.
determinism.seed_recipe: stable_seed(text) = int(md5(text)[:8], 16) -- NOT builtin hash() (salted by PYTHONHASHSEED)
guarantees: same seed -> same stream within and across processes
lattice iteration order is row-major (stable SVG bytes)

boundary_guard._comment: ref_frame consumes procedural_canonical.layout, so the package must stay a stdlib-only leaf to avoid a cycle and to be auditable.

migration_map._comment: Behaviour-preserving: every 'from' must reproduce its 'to' byte/value-for-value.
migration_map.M2_ref_frame_rows: ref_frame.rows(n, y0, total, h_gap) -> layout.stacks(n, y0, total, h_gap)

not_migrated.svg_art._scatter: hard-coded point list, not a regular lattice
not_migrated.svg_art._cross_hatch: clipped diagonal families, not a regular lattice
not_migrated.svg_art._spiral: polar spiral, not a regular lattice
